title: Checkpoint: The Restless Earth
objective: After this level you can explain how moving plates build mountains and cause earthquakes, volcanoes and tsunamis.
summary: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where two plates pull apart about 2 cm a year, and over a hotspot. Every kind of plate boundary builds something, and shakes something.

cards.headline: In Iceland, you can stand in the gap between two tectonic plates.
cards.body: Almost all of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge is hidden under the sea. In Iceland it comes up for air, and it's a perfect place to review the whole chapter.

cards.headline: The Atlantic's seam, on land
cards.body: Iceland is splitting as the North American and Eurasian plates pull apart, about 2 cm a year. At Þingvellir, the land between them has sunk into a rift valley about 7 km wide. Iceland's volcanoes get a double supply: the spreading ridge, plus a hotspot beneath it, like the one under Level 15's Hawaii. The island is Level 12's divergent boundary with a view.

cards.headline: Every boundary builds something, and shakes something

items.label: Pulling apart
points: New crust and rift valleys, as in Iceland

items.label: Pushing together
points: Sinking plates feed the Ring of Fire's volcanoes
Undersea quakes there launch Pacific tsunamis
If neither plate sinks: the Himalayas

cards.headline: Chapter 2 complete
learned: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and a hotspot
Plates there pull apart about 2 cm a year
Colliding plates build mountains and feed volcanoes
Sliding and sinking plates cause quakes and tsunamis

questions.prompt: Why is Iceland slowly splitting in two?

options.label: Two plates are colliding beneath it
It sits where two plates pull apart
Glaciers are carving it in half
options.rationale: Ice erodes it, but the split is tectonic.

options.label: The ocean is eroding a channel through it

questions.explanation: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where the North American and Eurasian plates pull apart about 2 cm a year.

questions.prompt: At Þingvellir, what has happened to the land between the separating plates?

options.label: It sank into a rift valley
It rose into a mountain range
options.rationale: That happens when plates push together.

options.label: It slid sideways along a fault
It dove under one of the plates
options.rationale: Nothing dives here: the plates pull apart.

questions.explanation: As the plates pull apart, the land between them sinks, forming a rift valley about 7 km wide.

questions.prompt: From Level 17: two plates push together, and neither can sink under the other. What forms?

options.label: A rift valley
options.rationale: That forms where plates pull apart.

options.label: A chain of hotspot islands
options.rationale: That's a plate moving over a hotspot.

options.label: A mountain range like the Himalayas
A new ocean
options.rationale: Oceans open where plates pull apart.

questions.explanation: With nowhere to sink, the crust crumples and thrusts upward, as it did when India met Eurasia.

questions.prompt: From Level 16: why do so many tsunamis start around the Pacific?

options.label: The Pacific has the strongest tides
options.rationale: Tides have little to do with tsunamis.

options.label: Its plates pull apart and open new crust
options.rationale: The Pacific rim is mostly plates pushing together.

options.label: Hurricanes there push water onto the coast
Ocean plates dive under others, setting off undersea quakes

questions.explanation: Around the Pacific, dense ocean plates slide under lighter ones. The undersea quakes there shove the seafloor and launch tsunamis.

questions.prompt: Iceland and Hawaii are both volcanic islands. What do they have in common?

options.label: Both sit on the Ring of Fire
options.rationale: Neither does: Iceland is in the Atlantic, Hawaii mid-plate.

options.label: Both are fed by a hotspot
Both sit where plates collide
options.rationale: Iceland's plates pull apart; Hawaii is far from any edge.

options.label: Both ride the Pacific Plate
options.rationale: Iceland sits on the Atlantic's ridge.

questions.explanation: Hawaii grew over a hotspot mid-plate. Iceland has one too, beneath the spreading Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
